correctness.rationale: All \(7140\) unordered Ulam distances in \(S_5\) were reconstructed independently from longest-common-subsequence dynamic programming and shortest paths in the single-translocation graph. Exhaustive four-clique enumeration gives exactly \(4020\) candidates, and every such clique has empty common-neighbor intersection, excluding size \(5\). The \(134\) identity-containing maxima satisfy the independent incidence identity \(4020\cdot4=134\cdot120\). Every maximum has distance profile \((3,3,3,3,3,3)\), and the full order-\(240\) natural-group orbit partition is recomputed directly. The packaged verifier was replayed successfully from its final path.

value.rationale: The parameter \(n=5,d=3\) is explicitly singled out in the 2015 literature as a small case where the proposed integer program improves the Singleton bound but still does not attain the true optimum. The equality census is therefore tied to a motivated classical benchmark rather than an arbitrary slice. The result adds substantive extremizer structure: all \(4020\) maxima are equidistant yet split into \(24\) natural symmetry types, providing exact benchmark data for Ulam/translocation-code algorithms and structural studies.
